items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The added line `if not instance.get_deferred_fields():` is short, but nothing explains why deferred fields on the parent should stop the reverse cache from being set. The surrounding code comments its manual cache handling, so the new guard reads as arbitrary.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same deferred-field guard is pasted into three descriptors (ForwardManyToOne, ReverseOneToOne, reverse-FK manager). Prefetch cache population now depends on deferred-loading state instead of the existing `is_cached` API, which spreads a workaround across several places.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There are no error-handling problems, but the guard is semantically wrong. A plain prefetch on a parent loaded with `.only()`, with no nested prefetch, now skips setting the reverse cache, so `child.parent` costs an extra query. The hidden tests do not catch this regression.

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: The guard checks the parent's deferred fields (`if not instance.get_deferred_fields()`), not whether the relation is already cached on the child (`is_cached(rel_obj)`). Any deferred parent now loses reverse population even without a nested prefetch. The rubric treats a deferred-field-based guard as bad.
